note: Illustrative example. The library 'tinycsv', its URLs and this bug are fictional; the format is real.

problem.title: Trailing empty field is dropped when a row ends with the delimiter and the file uses CRLF line endings
problem.symptom: Rows ending in ';' are returned with one field fewer than the header. No error is raised by tinycsv; the user's code failed later because column counts did not match.
problem.root_cause: The 3.1.0 fast path calls rstrip('\r\n' + delimiter) instead of rstrip('\r\n'), so a final empty field after the delimiter is removed together with the line ending. LF-only files take a different code path and are unaffected.

failed_attempts.approach: Open the file with newline='' as recommended for CSV parsing
failed_attempts.result: Test still fails: last field missing
Test still fails: argument is ignored on the fast path

reproduction.test_code:
import io
import tinycsv

def test_trailing_empty_field_crlf():
    data = 'a;b;c\r\n1;2;\r\n'
    rows = list(tinycsv.reader(io.StringIO(data, newline=''), delimiter=';'))
    assert rows == [['a', 'b', 'c'], ['1', '2', '']]

fix.description: Strip only the line terminator, never the delimiter. Workaround for users until a release ships: pin tinycsv==3.0.4, or normalize CRLF to LF before parsing.
fix.patch:
--- a/tinycsv/_fast.py
+++ b/tinycsv/_fast.py
@@ -88,2 +88,2 @@ def _split_line(line, delimiter):
-    line = line.rstrip('\r\n' + delimiter)
+    line = line.rstrip('\r\n')
     return line.split(delimiter)
